context:
Goal: re-importing an updated CSV keeps your received marks and leaves the order data right.
Problem (rule): the invariant record imports-merge-never-replace says a re-import "adds or refreshes entries by key", but the code (src/merge-rules.mjs, mergeItems, line 48) only adds new keys and keeps an existing line as is. A tracked line never moves to canceled on re-import, so a canceled order stays in your counts and may raise lost-mail flags. Your word decides which is right.
Based on (read): invariants/imports-merge-never-replace.md ("adds or refreshes entries by key"); src/merge-rules.mjs:48 and src/app.jsx:3908 (the base copy wins a key collision).
Based on (read): docs/decisions/orderwand-csv.md line 18 (a cancellation is Shipping Status = canceled, held in the item's tracking field; the key is order id, item number and product id, with no status); decision canceled-orders-leave-the-list (a canceled line leaves the list). The CSV record names no refund field, and the app's refunded stamp is your own mark.
Based on (measured): a dry run of the 2026-11-15 CSV against the live ledger shows 514 stored lines whose tracking differs from the file (coordinator, 2026-11-15 13:24 CST). Nobody knows whether the export shows refunds at all.
Departs from: main, where a changed line is ignored on re-import — option b updates the tracking field of a tracked line.
Meanwhile: lane reimport-received-pin builds the test that received marks survive a re-import. It holds only the wording change.

lastAnswer.note: Owner in chat, 13:38 CST (relayed by the coordinator): option b, refresh only the tracking field on a stored line whose key is already stored; never touch received marks or any other field.

options.gain: No app change, and a line on screen never shifts.
options.how: The record is reworded to say a re-import only adds new lines and keeps existing ones as they are.
options.label: Keep the code, fix the record
options.lose: A changed line in a newer CSV never updates, so a canceled order stays in your counts and may raise lost-mail flags.

options.gain: A cancellation in a newer CSV reaches the app, and the canceled order leaves your counts and lost-mail flags.
options.how: On a re-import, a tracked line gets its tracking value updated from the newer CSV. Received marks and every other field stay as they are.
options.label: Refresh changed lines on re-import
options.lose: An app change (builder, reviewer, Mac run), and a price or quantity change in a newer CSV still does not update.
options.note: Now means: narrowed. A re-import updates only the tracking field on a tracked line, so a cancellation moves it to the canceled section. It never touches received marks or any other field.

ref: invariant imports-merge-never-replace (a re-import keeps every item and adds or refreshes entries by key); step reimport-received-pin (the lane that tests received marks survive a re-import); src/merge-rules.mjs mergeItems (the merge the CSV import calls)
reply: Answered b at 13:38 CST in chat: a re-import refreshes only the tracking field on a stored line, and never touches received marks or any other field. Home is lane reimport-received-pin; the coordinator routes it.

shown.label: Keep the code, fix the record

title: When you re-import a newer CSV, should a changed order line, such as a cancellation in a newer CSV, update or stay as first imported?
why: 514 stored lines differ from the newest CSV in tracking alone, so the cost is real today. Updating only the tracking field on a stored line fixes that without touching received marks or any other field.
